scenes.text: Imagine standing in a beautiful, dense forest where the law literally doesn't apply to you, hidden deep inside Yellowstone National Park’s mysterious and creepy fifty-square-mile strip known as the Zone of Death.

Thanks to a truly bizarre and terrifying loophole in the United States Constitution, if you committed a major crime in this specific area, it might be legally impossible for authorities to prosecute you.
The Sixth Amendment guarantees your right to a jury from the state and district where the crime happened, but since this Idaho strip is completely uninhabited, a legal jury can never be formed.
It remains a shocking and unresolved blind spot in the American justice system, so would you ever dare to camp in this lawless wilderness? Comment your thoughts below and follow for more.
